name: The Mako
in_book: Named after the shark. Wide and flat at the back, V-hull forward, draws almost no water. The workhorse for client trips and the Pavilion Key escape.
facts: Mako Marine has built center consoles since 1967; a 17–19 ft Mako is the classic Florida guide boat.
Center console = room to walk all the way around during a fish fight.

name: The Bonefisher
in_book: 'The new smaller backcountry boat.' Towed behind the Sea Belle; tows the Sea Belle off the oyster bar; dragged across a channel by a grouper.

name: The Sea Belle
in_book: Four times the size of the Mako, with a cabin, bunks, kitchen, and a covered rear deck. 'Only he drives this here boat.' Home for a week at Lostman's River.

name: Dad's red airboat
in_book: Fire-engine red hull, white bow, 'just the right amount of rust.' Wrecked in the accident, found in a junkyard by Snapper, restored by Dan. Matt's sixteenth-birthday gift and next summer's project.
facts: An aircraft-style propeller pushes the flat-bottomed hull over inches of water and sawgrass.
Airboats need a full driver's license in Florida — hence the DMV trip.
Everglades airboats are loud: ear protection is standard.

name: Dan's Chevy Tahoe
in_book: Rusty, beloved, with the radio antenna Matt threatens to bend. Matt drives it to the DMV and to the airport.

name: Doc's skiff
in_book: 'Too little to be out so far from civilization.' Drifts up empty to the Sea Belle.

name: The smugglers' seaplane
in_book: Lands without lights at Little Pavilion Key and flashes three times.

name: The smugglers' jet boat
in_book: Faster than the Mako but can't follow into one-foot bays — 'bogged down in the muddy shallow bay' three times.

name: Boeing 737
in_book: Matt's first flight; starboard confirmed in the Guidebook.

name: Two boats and a car at South Point
